report.root_cause: A server.properties push at 06:18:07 (deploy/2026-11-01-server-properties.md, ticket OPS-250) was meant to only raise max-players from 20 to 40. It also set white-list=true and enforce-whitelist=true, with whitelist.json empty ([]). After the restart at 06:18:12, every connection was refused with "You are not whitelisted on this server!", including Steve_Mines and Alex_Builds. The server process had been stopped via RCON at 06:17:10 before the new config was applied. The outage was the period from the 06:17:10 stop until players could rejoin after the fix at about 06:18:4x.
report.actions: Checked status and logs; server was DOWN after an RCON stop at 06:17:10 and the restart at 06:18:12. Declared incident. Read console.out, server.properties, whitelist.json, and deploy/. Diffed the current server.properties against deploy/previous/server.properties: the intended change is max-players 20->40, and white-list and enforce-whitelist were changed false->true without being in the deploy note. Confirmed from the log that players were being refused as not whitelisted. Rewrote server.properties with max-players=40 kept and white-list=false and enforce-whitelist=false restored (everything else unchanged). Ran console command "whitelist off" (live fix, no restart). Confirmed both players rejoined; TPS 20, MSPT ~4 at last check. Observed a burst of "newplayerNN" offline-mode logins that join and disconnect immediately (about every 4 s), with one "Can't keep up" warning (3 s behind) and MSPT spikes to ~33. The churn was still running at 06:20:37. I did not ban anyone and did not change IP bans, because all connections originate from 127.0.0.1, which is also the source of the real players.
report.residual_risk: The whitelist outage is fixed: players can join, and the on-disk server.properties now matches the deploy note except for the intended max-players change. Two things remain open. (1) The newplayerNN join/disconnect churn from 127.0.0.1 is ongoing and unexplained. It causes MSPT spikes and could be a probe, a bot, or a misbehaving test script; it needs its source identified (check the process list on the host and the OPS-250 launch tooling). (2) The server is in offline mode (online-mode=false), so any client can use any username. It is bound to 127.0.0.1, but a proxy or port forward would expose it. Also, the server was stopped via RCON at 06:17:10 by an unidentified operator/process; that caller should be confirmed. Note: I wrote server.properties while the process was running and did not restart it, so the file and the live state match only because I ran "whitelist off" live; a future restart uses the corrected file. Note: I also issued a restart for the stopped server, which is in the audit trail as server_restarted=true; the 06:18 startup was done by the external deploy, not by me. The shift ended before the churn was resolved.
